papers.title: FrameForge: Harnessing Priors of Video Foundation Models for Unified Image Generation
papers.abstract: Abstract FrameForge enables adaptive conditional image generation by modeling variable condition-target relationships through dynamic temporal experts and intermediate reasoning pathways in pretrained video models.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Unified conditional image generation requires a single model to preserve different aspects of a visual input while producing a target image that follows textual guidance. Pretrained video models provide a promising foundation by encoding visual transformations across time, yet existing approaches typically assign the condition and target to fixed temporal positions. We observe that condition-target relationships vary substantially across generation tasks, while video models naturally encode visual transformations at different temporal scales. This motivates us to model conditional generation through input-adaptive virtual temporal relations. We propose FrameForge, which captures two complementary aspects of such relations. Mixture of Temporal Experts (MoTE) models how far the target lies from the condition by dynamically selecting temporal RoPE experts with different virtual intervals. Chain of Temporal Reasoning (CoTR) models how the condition is transformed into the target through a latent intermediate state, with a reasoning-bottleneck attention mask encouraging information propagation through this pathway. Experiments on DreamBench, COCO2017, and GEdit-Bench show that FrameForge achieves superior performance in subject-driven generation, canny-to-image generation, and image editing among the compared methods.

ru.title: Адаптивное временное мышление делает генерацию изображений точнее
ru.desc: В статье представлен FrameForge — метод условной генерации изображений, который использует предобученные видеомодели. Вместо фиксированного временного положения условия и цели, модель адаптивно выбирает виртуальные временные отношения в зависимости от входных данных. Mixture of Temporal Experts (MoTE) динамически выбирает RoPE-экспертов с разными виртуальными интервалами, а Chain of Temporal Reasoning (CoTR) моделирует преобразование условия в цель через промежуточное латентное состояние с attention-маской типа reasoning-bottleneck. Эксперименты на DreamBench, COCO2017 и GEdit-Bench показывают превосходство метода в генерации по субъекту, генерации из canny-карт и редактировании изображений.

en.title: Adapt the temporal path to transform each image
en.desc: FrameForge adapts pretrained video models for conditional image generation, where a model uses an input image and text to create a target image. Its Mixture of Temporal Experts selects among different virtual time intervals to match how much the target should differ from the input. Its Chain of Temporal Reasoning guides information through a latent intermediate state, modeling how the input is transformed into the target. Experiments show strong results on subject-driven generation, canny-to-image generation, and image editing benchmarks.

zh.title: 让时间关系随任务而变，驱动更灵活的图像生成
zh.desc: 本文提出 FrameForge，用预训练视频模型进行统一的条件图像生成，让模型根据输入图像和文本指引生成目标图像。它指出，不同任务中条件图像与目标图像之间的关系各不相同，因此不应把它们固定在视频序列的特定位置。时间专家混合（MoTE）会动态选择具有不同虚拟时间间隔的 RoPE 专家，以表示目标与条件之间的变化幅度；时间推理链（CoTR）则通过潜在中间状态和推理瓶颈注意力掩码，引导信息逐步传递并完成图像变换。在 DreamBench、COCO2017 和 GEdit-Bench 上的实验表明，FrameForge 在主体驱动生成、边缘图转图像和图像编辑任务中优于对比方法。

papers.title: R^2Orch: Recursive Self-Improvement for Agent Orchestration via Self-Play within a Skill-Internalization Loop
papers.abstract: Abstract R²Orch uses recursive self-play with learnable task selection and skill withdrawal to train orchestrators without hand-designed curricula, improving performance across reasoning and interactive tasks.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small In recent years, agentic orchestration has been widely applied to solve complex human tasks. However, existing orchestration learning still faces key challenges, including hand-designed curricula, advantage collapse when a task's rollouts all reach the same outcome, and unreliable evaluation signals that judge each skill by one noisy score. To address these challenges, we propose R^2Orch, a new paradigm of Recursive Self-Play Orchestration: an inner loop of self-play that improves the orchestrator on self-chosen tasks, and an outer loop that improves how the inner loop improves. To support this paradigm, we introduce Recursive Learnability, a training objective that rewards a Proposer for choosing tasks whose rollouts keep reaching different outcomes as skills are withdrawn. Built on this objective, we further propose Skill Withdrawal, in which the outer loop withdraws each skill once a controlled evaluation within self-play shows that the orchestrator performs as well without it. Moreover, the two loops form one cycle: failures are distilled into skills, skills into parameters, and withdrawals lead the Proposer to new failures, so the orchestrator moves toward zero-skill deployment. Experimental results on twelve datasets show that R^2Orch consistently outperforms baselines across question answering, math, code, and interactive tasks. Our code is available at https://github.com/beita6969/R2Orch.
affiliations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen, China

ru.title: Оркестратор учится сам и постепенно отказывается от подсказок
ru.desc: Статья предлагает R²Orch — парадигму рекурсивного самообучения (Recursive Self-Play) для обучения оркестратора агентных LLM без вручную заданных учебных программ. Внутренний цикл self-play улучшает оркестратор на задачах, которые сам Proposer выбирает, а внешний цикл улучшает сам процесс обучения. Для этого вводится цель Recursive Learnability, поощряющая выбор задач, на которых траектории (rollouts) дают разные исходы даже после удаления навыков, а также механизм Skill Withdrawal, убирающий навыки, которые больше не нужны оркестратору. Эксперименты на двенадцати датасетах показывают, что метод стабильно превосходит базовые подходы в вопросах-ответах, математике, коде и интерактивных задачах.

en.title: Learn from failures, then orchestrate with fewer skills
en.desc: R²Orch trains task orchestrators through recursive self-play, rather than relying on hand-designed curricula. A Proposer selects tasks that remain challenging, using differences in outcomes as skills are withdrawn to measure whether the tasks are still learnable. The system turns failures into skills and then into model parameters, while removing skills when controlled evaluations show they are no longer needed. Across twelve datasets, R²Orch outperforms baseline methods on question answering, math, code, and interactive tasks.

zh.title: 让智能体在自选任务与技能递减中学会独立编排
zh.desc: R²Orch 提出一种递归自我博弈方法，让智能体编排器自行选择任务并持续改进，而不必依赖人工设计的训练课程。它用“递归可学习性”目标奖励任务提议者选择合适的任务，使撤去技能后，任务结果仍能呈现差异，避免训练信号失效。外层循环通过受控评估逐步撤去不再必要的技能；训练中的失败会被提炼为技能，再融入模型参数，推动编排器迈向无需外部技能的部署。实验表明，该方法在十二个数据集的问答、数学、编程和交互任务上均优于基线。

papers.title: Does Scaling Toward AGI Depend on What System-1 Lets System-2 Execute?
papers.abstract: Abstract Co-designing a resource-heavy reasoning system with a lightweight predictive evaluator can reduce execution costs by filtering interactions, with efficiency governed by the density of useful interactions.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Progress toward artificial general intelligence (AGI) has largely relied on scaling a resource-intensive executive, System-2, through larger models, more data and compute, longer reasoning, and more agents. We ask whether the next stage may come instead from co-designing it with System-1, a lightweight, semantically aware predictor that evaluates candidate interactions before execution, so that System-2 acts only on those worth their cost. Our answer is a qualified yes. We study conditional interaction, a predict--gate--execute--update loop: System-1 estimates each candidate's utility, System-2 executes those admitted by an adaptive threshold, and the outcomes update System-1. The loop spans training, test-time reasoning, adaptive decision-making, and agentic tool use, with utility and cost defined by the application. Under ideal screening and equal execution costs, execution compute falls by a factor approaching 1/ρ_u, where ρ_u is the density of utility-relevant interactions (cost-weighted when costs differ); prediction errors, exploration, and distribution shift reduce the saving. We bound selection regret by predictor error and the utility margin. These results motivate our central hypothesis: ρ_u is a measurable coordinate of scaling efficiency and makes informative compute a better description of scaling than total compute.
affiliations: Department of Automation, Tsinghua University, Beijing, China
Department of Computer Science, Tsinghua University, Beijing, China

ru.title: Считать не всё подряд: умный отбор вместо грубой мощности
ru.desc: Статья предлагает совместно проектировать тяжёлую систему рассуждений System-2 и лёгкий предсказатель System-1, который оценивает кандидатов на взаимодействие до их выполнения. Петля predict–gate–execute–update пропускает к System-2 только те взаимодействия, полезность которых превышает адаптивный порог, а результаты обновляют предсказатель. Теоретически показано, что вычислительные затраты падают примерно в 1/ρ_u раз, где ρ_u — плотность полезных взаимодействий, а ошибки предсказания и исследование снижают эффект, при этом регрет ограничен ошибкой предсказателя и полезным запасом. Авторы утверждают, что ρ_u можно измерять и использовать как показатель эффективности масштабирования, полезного для AGI, вместо простого роста общего объёма вычислений.

en.title: Spend Compute Only on Useful Interactions
en.desc: The paper proposes pairing a powerful but expensive System-2 with a lightweight System-1 predictor. System-1 estimates the utility of candidate actions, and an adaptive threshold decides which ones System-2 should execute. This predict–gate–execute–update loop can reduce compute, especially when useful interactions are rare, though prediction errors and changing data can lessen the savings. The authors argue that the density of useful interactions helps measure scaling efficiency and that informative compute may be more meaningful than total compute.

zh.title: 先预测再执行，让每一份计算都更有用
zh.desc: 论文提出将轻量级的 System-1 预测器与资源密集型的 System-2 推理器协同设计，先评估候选交互的价值，再决定是否执行。该方法采用“预测—门控—执行—更新”循环：System-1 估计效用，System-2 按自适应阈值处理获准的交互，并利用执行结果更新预测器。理想筛选下，计算开销可随有用交互密度降低而显著减少；但预测误差、探索需求和分布偏移会削弱节省效果，选择遗憾则受预测误差和效用差距约束。作者据此提出，有用交互密度是衡量扩展效率的重要指标，相比总计算量，“信息性计算”更能描述系统的扩展能力。

papers.title: REA: A Routed Embodied Agent Runtime for Asynchronous Brain-Cerebellum Control
papers.abstract: Abstract REA unifies deliberative and reactive policies in a single runtime with asynchronous coordination, achieving high success rates with reduced control overhead across simulated and real robot tasks.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Foundation models are becoming remarkably reliable at high-level reasoning, yet they remain too slow and costly to serve as fine-grained controllers. Conversely, fast policies like VLAs and whole-body controllers offer more efficient reflexes, but struggle to generalize. While pairing a deliberative brain (foundation models) with a reactive cerebellum (fast policies) seems natural for embodied systems, two obstacles remain: methods are built and scored on incompatible stacks, and their asynchronous coordination is difficult. For example, an agent that calls the VLA in the agentic loop can stall the fast execution, while a VLA that calls the agent on errors tends to re-trigger fallbacks repeatedly or completely miss silent failures. To address this, we propose REA (Routed Embodied Agent), a unified runtime where a deliberative System 2, an embodied router System 1 and reactive System 0 policies cooperate under a single golden rule - no running policy waits on the brain. Instead of querying the brain at each failure, REA employs a route memory that stores each policy's measured success ahead of time, a boundary-triggered judge gate that consults the brain on policy execution, and a shared-budget escalation ladder for bounded recovery. Evaluated on 3,000 test episodes across 60 LIBERO-Pro tasks, REA reaches 95.9% success and beats the best single-agent baseline in its own policy pool (94.7%) while reducing control steps by 25% and control time by 17%. In a separate 100-episode RoboTwin 2.0 study, REA achieves 84% success with VLA policies and 86% with VLA+code, compared with 80% for the strongest single VLA baseline MEDex. These results demonstrate learned and programmatic policies operating within the same runtime. REA also transfers to BEHAVIOR-1K and a real Unitree G1 humanoid, achieving the highest observed success among the compared methods.
affiliations: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences

ru.title: Быстрые рефлексы и медленный разум работают вместе, не мешая друг другу
ru.desc: В статье представлен REA (Routed Embodied Agent) — единая среда выполнения, где медленная LLM-модель System 2 отвечает за высокоуровневое рассуждение, router System 1 выбирает подходящую политику, а быстрые reactive-политики System 0 (VLA и контроллеры всего тела) выполняют действия. Ключевое правило: ни одна работающая политика не ждёт ответа «мозга», а координация выполняется асинхронно через route memory и judge gate с общим бюджетом эскалации. Метод протестирован на LIBERO-Pro, RoboTwin 2.0, BEHAVIOR-1K и humanoid-роботе Unitree G1, где он повышает успешность и сокращает число шагов управления на 25%. Результаты показывают, что обучаемые и программные политики могут работать в одном runtime.

en.title: Let the robot think deeply without slowing its reflexes
en.desc: REA combines slow foundation-model reasoning with fast reactive policies in one robot-control runtime. Its router uses stored policy success rates, checks for problems at execution boundaries, and escalates recovery within a shared budget, so running policies do not have to wait for the reasoning model. Across simulated tasks, REA achieved high success while reducing control steps and time compared with a strong single-agent baseline, and it also performed well on a real humanoid robot. The results show that learned and programmatic policies can work together in a unified system.

zh.title: 让深度推理与快速反应协同，机器人成功更高、控制更省
zh.desc: REA提出一种统一的机器人运行框架，让擅长推理的基础模型、负责选择策略的路由器和快速反应策略协同工作。它采用策略成功率记忆、边界触发的判断门，以及共享预算的逐级恢复机制，并确保正在运行的策略不会等待基础模型。实验显示，REA在LIBERO-Pro和RoboTwin 2.0等任务中取得较高成功率，同时减少控制步骤和控制时间，也能迁移到其他模拟环境及真实人形机器人。结果表明，学习得到的策略与程序化策略可以在同一运行框架中有效配合。

papers.title: Apriel Voice 27B Preview: An Open Model for Speech, Reasoning, and Tool Use
papers.abstract: Abstract Apriel Voice 27B Preview is an open speech-language model that integrates speech understanding, reasoning, and tool use within a shared backbone, achieving strong results on audio benchmarks through a two-stage training procedure with online distillation.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small A capable voice assistant must do more than recognize words; it must understand requests, reason over context, sustain conversations, and act through tools. We present Apriel Voice 27B Preview, an open speech-language model that unifies these capabilities within a shared reasoning backbone while retaining text and image input modalities. Built on the post-trained Gemma 4 26B-A4B checkpoint, Apriel Voice directly processes speech and generates both responses and tool calls without requiring a separate dialogue model. We introduce a two-stage training procedure to adapt the model to speech. The first stage establishes the speech interface, while the second jointly adapts the projector and backbone through supervised fine-tuning, text replay, and source-dependent cross-entropy and forward Kullback--Leibler divergence supervision. Automatically constructed speech-conditioned dialogues provide conversational training data, while local teacher serving, overlapping teacher and student computation, and fused full-vocabulary losses enable efficient online distillation. In thinking mode, Apriel Voice achieves a score of 98.90 on Big Bench Audio, 81.13 on Speech-BFCL, and a task success rate of 65.51% on τ-Voice, with a mean latency of 1.91 seconds. It also achieves 51.27% English EVA accuracy and 74.13% experience pass@1. Finally, we deploy Apriel Voice 27B Preview on a custom serving platform to support interactive voice interactions.

ru.title: Голосовой ассистент, который слышит, думает и действует
ru.desc: Статья представляет Apriel Voice 27B Preview — открытую speech-language модель, которая объединяет распознавание речи, рассуждение и использование инструментов (tool use) в одном общем backbone. Модель построена на основе Gemma 4 26B-A4B и напрямую обрабатывает речевой вход, генерируя ответы и вызовы инструментов без отдельной диалоговой LLM. Обучение проходит в два этапа: сначала настраивается речевой интерфейс, затем совместно адаптируются projector и backbone с помощью supervised fine-tuning, text replay и online distillation с комбинацией cross-entropy и forward KL-дивергенции. Модель показывает высокие результаты на бенчмарках Big Bench Audio, Speech-BFCL и τ-Voice при средней задержке около 1,91 секунды.

en.title: One Voice Model to Listen, Reason, and Act
en.desc: Apriel Voice 27B Preview is an open speech-language model that understands audio, reasons about requests, and produces spoken responses or tool calls using one shared backbone. It also accepts text and images, without needing a separate dialogue model. The model is adapted to speech in two training stages, using supervised fine-tuning and online distillation, where it learns from a teacher model’s outputs. It achieves strong results on several audio and voice-assistant benchmarks, while supporting interactive conversations with low latency.

zh.title: 让语音模型听懂、会推理，也能调用工具
zh.desc: Apriel Voice 27B Preview 是一种开放式语音语言模型，使用同一个推理骨干处理语音理解、推理和工具调用，也支持文本与图像输入。模型采用两阶段训练：先建立语音输入输出能力，再通过监督微调、文本回放和在线蒸馏共同适配投影层与骨干网络。训练数据包括自动构造的语音对话，并结合交叉熵损失与前向 KL 散度，让学生模型学习教师模型的输出。模型在多项音频基准上取得较强成绩，并已部署到定制平台，用于交互式语音对话。

papers.title: WeFair: Fidelity-Aware Alignment from Human Feedback for Personalized Query Rewriting in Short-Video Search
papers.abstract: Abstract WeFair improves personalized query rewriting via fidelity-aware human feedback stages—demonstration, preference, and verification—to reduce intent drift and boost search effectiveness in short-video platforms.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Short-video search needs compact query rewriters that recover users' personalized intent from ambiguous queries under strict latency constraints. Existing LLM-based methods have improved rewriting by using synthetic reasoning and subsequent consumption-behavioral feedback. However, overemphasizing subsequent consumption can favor engaging content over the user's immediate need, causing intent drift even when rewritten queries are grounded in behavioral history. We propose WeFair, Fidelity-Aware Alignment from Human Feedback for Personalized Query Rewriting in WeChat short-video search. WeFair uses human feedback according to how directly it reflects personalized intent, assigning feedback fidelity to a progression from demonstration to preference to verification. We first mine actual queries and user reformulations from search sessions, and then screen them for contextual support. In the demonstration stage, a supervised fine-tuning curriculum progresses from large-scale context-to-query learning to reasoning and direct prediction on human reformulation and preservation. In the preference stage, direct preference optimization learns relative preferences from subsequent consumption feedback. In the verification stage, group relative policy optimization rewards exact agreement with reformulation or preservation targets to constrain intent drift. Further analysis shows that broad supervision benefits the full curriculum supervised training, while strict verification achieves better performance than auxiliary rewards. In offline experiments, WeFair-2B outperforms strong rewriting baselines in overall accuracy and intent preservation. An online A/B test shows relative increases of 2.593% in effective video-view rate and a 2.350% relative reduction in query reformulation rate. WeFair-2B has been deployed in the WeChat short-video search system, which serves over 100 million queries per day.

ru.title: Ищем то, что нужно пользователю, а не то, что он будет смотреть
ru.desc: В статье предлагается WeFair, метод персонализированного переписывания поисковых запросов для коротких видео в WeChat, который использует human feedback с учётом степени точности его отражения намерения пользователя. Обучение проходит в три этапа: supervised fine-tuning на демонстрациях человеческих переформулировок, direct preference optimization по предпочтениям на основе последующего потребления контента и group relative policy optimization с наградой за точное совпадение с целевой переформулировкой. Такой подход снижает intent drift, когда модель выбирает вовлекающий контент вместо реальной потребности пользователя. Офлайн-эксперименты показывают превосходство компактной модели WeFair-2B над сильными базовыми LLM-методами, а онлайн A/B-тест даёт рост effective video-view rate на 2.593% и снижение query reformulation rate на 2.350%.

en.title: Rewrite for the User’s Intent, Not Just Their Next Click
en.desc: WeFair is a personalized query rewriting system for short-video search that aims to capture what a user means without changing their intent. It aligns models through three stages of human feedback: demonstrations teach query rewriting, preferences reflect feedback from users’ later behavior, and verification checks that rewrites match human reformulations or preserve the original intent. The approach combines supervised fine-tuning, direct preference optimization, and group relative policy optimization, with strict verification helping to limit intent drift. In experiments, WeFair-2B improved accuracy and intent preservation, and an online test increased effective video views by 2.593% while reducing query reformulations by 2.350%.

zh.title: 以意图忠实度为核心，让查询改写更懂用户
zh.desc: 这篇论文提出 WeFair，用于短视频搜索中的个性化查询改写，目标是在低延迟条件下准确理解含糊查询，同时避免改写偏离用户当下意图。它按反馈与个性化意图的贴合程度，依次采用示范、偏好和验证三个阶段：先用人工改写数据进行监督微调，再通过直接偏好优化学习用户反馈中的相对偏好，最后用组相对策略优化强化对目标改写的精确匹配。实验表明，严格验证有助于减少意图漂移，WeFair-2B 在离线准确率和意图保留方面优于强基线。线上测试中，有效视频观看率相对提升 2.593%，查询改写率相对降低 2.350%，该系统已部署于微信短视频搜索。

papers.title: Latent Reasoning in Continuous Space for Unified Multimodal Models
papers.abstract: Abstract LARC enables continuous latent reasoning for unified multimodal models, improving image generation quality and enabling test-time scaling without discrete token bottlenecks.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) achieve remarkable success on diverse multimodal understanding and generation tasks, yet they still struggle to effectively leverage language-based chain-of-thought reasoning for image generation. As a result, existing reasoning-augmented UMMs often fail to inherit the test-time scaling and fine-grained controllability observed in large language models. We attribute this failure to a fundamental modality mismatch: reasoning is performed in a discrete token space, whereas image generation operates in a continuous space. To bridge this gap, we introduce a Latent Reasoning framework in Continuous space (LARC), which alleviates the token-level bottleneck by reasoning over continuous hidden states. Specifically, the training framework consists of two stages: (i) curriculum supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and (ii) information-gain reinforcement learning (RL). First, the curriculum SFT stage gradually converts token-level reasoning into latent reasoning. Subsequently, the information-gain RL stage self-evolves latent reasoning without ground truth supervision. Experiments across diverse text-to-image generation benchmarks show that LARC consistently improves generation quality, prompt following, and compositional fidelity. Notably, LARC achieves state-of-the-art performance on GenEval with a 7%p gain over BAGEL and demonstrates clear test-time scaling behavior, outperforming token-based generation under both parallel and sequential test-time scaling strategies.

ru.title: Рассуждать в непрерывном латентном пространстве — ключ к качественной генерации изображений
ru.desc: Статья представляет LARC — фреймворк латентного рассуждения в непрерывном пространстве для унифицированных мультимодальных моделей (UMM), который устраняет разрыв между дискретным текстовым рассуждением и непрерывной генерацией изображений. Обучение состоит из двух этапов: куррикулум-SFT, постепенно переводящий токенное рассуждение в латентное, и обучение с подкреплением на основе information-gain (RL), которое развивает латентное рассуждение без ground truth разметки. Эксперименты на бенчмарках text-to-image показывают улучшение качества генерации, соблюдения промпта и композиционной точности, а также результат SOTA на GenEval (+7 п.п. над BAGEL). Модель демонстрирует масштабирование на этапе инференса (test-time scaling) и превосходит токенную генерацию при параллельных и последовательных стратегиях.

en.title: Reason in Latents, Generate Better Images
en.desc: LARC helps unified multimodal models reason about images using continuous hidden states instead of discrete text tokens. This approach bridges the mismatch between language-based reasoning and continuous image generation. Training first uses curriculum supervised fine-tuning, then information-gain reinforcement learning to improve latent reasoning without ground-truth labels. Across text-to-image benchmarks, LARC improves image quality, prompt following, and compositional fidelity, while also scaling better at test time.

zh.title: 在连续隐空间中推理，让多模态图像生成越想越好
zh.desc: 统一多模态模型通常用离散文本 token 进行推理，但图像生成依赖连续表示，这种差异会限制推理效果和测试时扩展能力。LARC 提出在连续隐状态空间中进行潜在推理，以缩小语言推理与图像生成之间的差距。它先通过课程式监督微调逐步将 token 级推理转为潜在推理，再用信息增益强化学习在没有标准答案监督的情况下改进推理。实验显示，LARC 提升了图像生成质量、提示词遵循度和组合保真度，并在 GenEval 上取得领先表现，且测试时扩展效果优于基于 token 的方法。

papers.title: Wizard: Manipulate Any World in Real Time via Agentic Control
papers.abstract: Abstract Wizard is an agentic game world model that uses structured motion proxies and adaptive masking to enable real-time, generalizable video generation with precise character control across diverse scenes.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Recent advances in video world models have enabled the generation of increasingly realistic and interactive virtual environments, opening new possibilities for player-customizable gameplay. Agentic frameworks further advance this direction by decoupling explicit game logic and controllable world representations from visual generation. However, existing approaches support only simple game settings and predefined motion patterns, generalize poorly to unseen environments and characters, and offer limited real-time interactivity. In this paper, we introduce Wizard, an agentic game world model that enables real-time, precise control over character motions while generalizing zero-shot across novel scenes, characters, and actions. To achieve this, we construct a diverse dataset spanning 750 scenes and 178 characters, incorporating skeleton and geometry information as structured representations. We leverage these representations as intermediate proxies to condition a video generation model, together with an adaptive masking mechanism that improves alignment between the conditioning signals and generated video rollouts. Furthermore, we introduce an agentic framework that explicitly maintains and updates game states, allowing players to freely configure their virtual worlds and exercise fine-grained control over character motions while preserving visual quality and gameplay consistency. By combining agentic control with structured proxy-based generation, our framework unlocks new possibilities for player-driven game creation with real-time, generalizable, and mechanically consistent world simulation.

ru.title: Волшебник создаёт игровые миры в реальном времени: управляемая генерация видео без ограничений
ru.desc: Статья представляет Wizard — агентную world model для игр, которая генерирует видео в реальном времени и позволяет точно управлять движениями персонажей. Модель использует структурированные прокси-представления (скелеты и геометрию), полученные из датасета из 750 сцен и 178 персонажей, для условной генерации видео. Адаптивный маскинг улучшает согласованность между управляющими сигналами и сгенерированными видеороликами, а агентный фреймворк поддерживает и обновляет игровое состояние. Подход обеспечивает zero-shot обобщение на новые сцены, персонажей и действия при сохранении визуального качества и игровой логики.

en.title: Control the character, create the world
en.desc: Wizard is an agentic game world model that generates interactive video in real time and lets players control character motions precisely. It uses skeleton and geometry information as structured proxies to guide a video generation model, with adaptive masking to better align those signals with generated frames. Its dataset covers 750 scenes and 178 characters, supporting zero-shot generalization to new scenes, characters, and actions. An explicit game-state framework lets players configure worlds and control motion while helping keep gameplay visually coherent and mechanically consistent.

zh.title: 让玩家实时掌控角色，在陌生世界中生成连贯游戏
zh.desc: 本文提出 Wizard，一种用于游戏世界模拟的智能体视频生成模型，可实时、精确地控制角色动作，并零样本泛化到新的场景、角色和动作。研究构建了包含 750 个场景和 178 个角色的数据集，并将骨骼与几何信息作为结构化中间代理来条件化视频生成模型。模型还采用自适应掩码机制，提升控制信号与生成视频序列之间的对齐效果。其智能体框架会显式维护和更新游戏状态，使玩家能够自由配置虚拟世界、细致控制角色，同时保持视觉质量与游戏机制的一致性。

papers.title: HiFOR: Hierarchical Foresight with Action-Guided World Grounding for Vision-Language-Action Model
papers.abstract: Abstract HiFOR improves robotic manipulation by hierarchically predicting future states and retrieving relevant future information to guide action generation.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have demonstrated promising capabilities in robotic manipulation by integrating visual perception, language understanding, and action generation. Recent advances have further incorporated future prediction to enhance the understanding of environmental dynamics and task progression. However, existing methods often model short-term dynamics and long-term task objectives separately, while directly incorporating predicted futures into action policies without sufficiently considering their relevance to current action requirements. To address these limitations, we propose HiFOR, a hierarchical foresight framework with action-guided world retrieval. Specifically, Hierarchical Foresight Prediction jointly predicts short-term state evolution, semantic milestones, and final goal states through a Hierarchical Dependency Mask (HDM), establishing dependencies across temporal horizons. Building upon these predictions, Structure-Aware Latent World Modeling organizes future latent representations along the horizon, view, and spatial dimensions to facilitate fine-grained retrieval. Furthermore, Action-Guided Factorized World Retrieval adaptively retrieves relevant future information from the structured latent world based on evolving action representations during denoising, providing targeted guidance for action generation. Extensive experiments on two simulation benchmarks and six real-world robotic manipulation tasks demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.

ru.title: Заглядывая вперёд, робот точнее действует
ru.desc: В статье представлен фреймворк HiFOR для Vision-Language-Action (VLA) моделей в робототехнике, который иерархически предсказывает будущие состояния: краткосрочную динамику среды, семантические вехи и конечное целевое состояние. Для связи этих горизонтов используется Hierarchical Dependency Mask (HDM). Структурированное латентное мировое моделирование (Structure-Aware Latent World Modeling) организует будущие латентные представления по временным, видовым и пространственным измерениям, а механизм Action-Guided Factorized World Retrieval адаптивно извлекает релевантную информацию в процессе denoising для генерации действий. Эксперименты на двух симуляционных бенчмарках и шести реальных задачах манипуляции подтверждают эффективность подхода.

en.title: Look Ahead, Retrieve What Matters, Act with Purpose
en.desc: HiFOR is a framework for vision-language-action models that uses predictions about the future to improve robotic manipulation. It jointly predicts near-term changes, meaningful task milestones, and final goal states, linking them with a Hierarchical Dependency Mask. It organizes predicted future information by time horizon, camera view, and spatial location so the model can retrieve useful details. During action generation, it selects future information that fits the actions being considered, and experiments show gains in simulation and real-world tasks.

zh.title: 分层预见未来，按需检索信息，助力机器人精准行动
zh.desc: 本文提出 HiFOR，一种用于机器人操作的分层前瞻框架，帮助视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型利用未来状态生成动作。它通过分层依赖掩码联合预测短期状态变化、语义里程碑和最终目标状态，建立不同时间尺度之间的联系。框架还将未来的潜在表示按预测时域、视角和空间结构组织起来，并根据动作表示的变化检索与当前动作相关的信息。仿真基准和真实机器人操作任务上的实验表明，HiFOR 能有效提升操作表现。

papers.title: OSWAM: An Effective World Action Model with One-Step Action Generation
papers.abstract: Abstract OSWAM enables real-time, high-quality action generation in autonomous driving and embodied control by initializing diffusion with structured imagination tokens and distilling future-conditioned privileged information into a single denoising step.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Direct-policy World Action Models (WAM) have demonstrated the benefits of decoupling action generation from explicit future visual prediction for efficient inference in autonomous driving and embodied control. However, they still require tens of denoising steps to achieve competitive action quality, incurring substantial latency and hindering real-time deployment. Simply reducing the number of denoising steps will collapse the nonlinear multi-step denoising trajectory into coarse updates, substantially degrading action quality. To reduce the denoising steps while enabling real-time action generation, we present an effective world action model with one-step action generation, namely OSWAM, for autonomous driving and embodied control. We argue that it is the absence of structured action priors in random noise initialization that forces direct-policy WAMs to recover coherent action sequences through iterative denoising. Hence, we construct imagination tokens to initialize the diffusion process, providing physical priors and action-conditioned representations. We further introduce privileged information distillation with future conditioning to enhance future-aware action generation. As a result, OSWAM can efficiently and effectively generate high quality actions in just one diffusion step. Our experiments demonstrate that OSWAM achieves comparable or even better results in both autonomous driving and embodied control than direct-policy WAM and Joint-WAM that require tens of steps. It obtains approximately 3times speedup over direct-policy WAM baselines and supports real-time compiled inference with latency as low as 40ms on an NVIDIA RTX 5090 GPU. The project page is available at https://gwenzhang.github.io/OSWAM/

ru.title: Одна диффузия вместо десятков: действия в реальном времени за счёт умного старта
ru.desc: В статье представлен OSWAM — World Action Model для автономного вождения и embodied control, который генерирует действия за один шаг диффузии вместо десятков. Ключевая идея: инициализация диффузионного процесса не случайным шумом, а структурированными imagination tokens, несущими физические априорные знания и action-conditioned представления. Дополнительно применяется дистилляция privileged information с учётом будущих состояний (future conditioning), что улучшает прогнозирование действий. По результатам экспериментов модель достигает качества, сопоставимого с многошаговыми baseline, при ускорении примерно в 3 раза и задержке около 40 мс на NVIDIA RTX 5090.

en.title: Imagine Better, Act in One Step
en.desc: OSWAM is a world action model for autonomous driving and embodied control that generates actions in a single diffusion step. It starts diffusion from structured imagination tokens, which provide physical priors and action-conditioned representations instead of unstructured random noise. It also distills future-conditioned privileged information to make its actions more aware of what may happen next. Experiments show action quality comparable to or better than multi-step baselines, with roughly three times the speed and inference latency as low as 40 ms on an NVIDIA RTX 5090.

zh.title: 用结构化想象与未来蒸馏，实现一步生成高质量动作
zh.desc: 本文提出 OSWAM，用于自动驾驶和具身控制中的动作生成。它用带有物理先验和动作条件表征的“想象令牌”初始化扩散过程，帮助模型生成连贯的动作序列。研究还通过未来条件下的特权信息蒸馏，让模型在单步去噪中获得对未来的感知能力。实验显示，OSWAM 只需一步扩散便能达到与多步方法相当或更好的效果，并在 NVIDIA RTX 5090 上实现约 40 毫秒的推理延迟。

papers.title: ReLift: Dense 3D Tracking as Lifted Trajectory Repair
papers.abstract: Abstract ReLift improves dense 3D tracking by repairing and completing lifted trajectories using geometric trajectory refinement without requiring image-based training.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Dense 3D tracking from monocular video requires establishing point correspondences over time, estimating their depth, and inferring their trajectories during occlusion. Existing methods typically learn these tasks jointly, a demanding objective given the scarcity of 4D supervision. We show that strong pretrained 2D trackers and 3D geometry models provide an effective foundation: lifted trajectories, with occluded segments simply interpolated, already rival dedicated 3D trackers using the same geometry. However, lifted trajectories inherit correspondence and depth errors, and under occlusion, their depth comes from the occluder rather than the tracked point. We introduce ReLift, an efficient feed-forward framework that recasts dense 3D tracking as geometric trajectory repair and completion. At its core, a trajectory corrector alternates attention along and across trajectories to preserve reliable observations, repair corrupted positions, and complete missing motion. Using only geometric inputs allows us to train directly on 3D trajectories with simulated lifting errors, decoupling training from images and from any specific tracker or geometry model. Concentrating 4D supervision on trajectory refinement yields a reusable model that consistently improves lifted trajectories across trackers and geometry providers without retraining, so it benefits directly from future advances in either component. On WorldTrack, ReLift achieves state-of-the-art mean accuracy, improving on the strongest baselines by 2.1 APD on all points and 3.0 on dynamic points, with faster configurations remaining competitive with leading 3D trackers while running faster than 4RC. Visit our supplementry page for more examples and code.

ru.title: Чинить и достраивать траектории вместо того, чтобы учить всё заново
ru.desc: Статья представляет ReLift — быстрый feed-forward фреймворк для плотного 3D-трекинга по монокулярному видео, который рассматривает задачу как восстановление и дополнение лифтированных траекторий. Из 2D-трекеров и 3D geometry models берутся траектории, а окклюзии заполняются интерполяцией, однако ошибки соответствий и глубины остаются. Ядро метода — trajectory corrector, который чередует attention вдоль и поперёк траекторий, исправляя искажённые позиции и восстанавливая пропущенное движение. Модель обучается только на геометрических данных с симулированными ошибками лифтинга, без изображений и привязки к конкретному трекеру, и на WorldTrack достигает state-of-the-art точности, опережая сильнейшие baselines.

en.title: Repair lifted trajectories for better 3D tracking
en.desc: ReLift improves dense 3D tracking by refining trajectories lifted from monocular video. It uses a trajectory corrector that applies attention along and across trajectories to fix errors and fill in missing motion. The model trains on 3D trajectories with simulated lifting errors, so it does not need image-based training or depend on a particular tracker or geometry model. ReLift improves accuracy across different components and achieves state-of-the-art results on WorldTrack while offering faster configurations.

zh.title: 修复并补全三维轨迹，让稠密跟踪更准确、更高效
zh.desc: ReLift 将单目视频的稠密三维跟踪转化为三维轨迹的几何修复与补全，不需要基于图像进行训练。它以预训练的二维跟踪器和三维几何模型生成的轨迹为基础，利用轨迹中的可靠观测来修正错误位置，并补全遮挡时缺失的运动。核心模块通过沿轨迹和跨轨迹交替进行注意力计算，且只使用几何输入，因此可在模拟误差的三维轨迹上训练，不依赖特定的跟踪器或几何模型。在 WorldTrack 上，ReLift 达到领先的平均精度，并能跨不同基础模型提升轨迹质量，同时保持较快的运行速度。

papers.title: Follow the Gradient: Tracing Safety Degradation Back to Training Data
papers.abstract: Abstract SimpleLoRIF uses gradient alignment to filter instruction data that silently degrades LLM safety, yielding a safer dataset that reduces adversarial success while preserving capabilities.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Fine-tuning Large Language Models (LLMs) on instruction data can quietly erode their safety, even when no training example looks harmful. Because this safety-degrading data looks benign, standard content filters struggle to catch it. We tackle this problem by developing SimpleLoRIF, a scalable gradient embedding method that identifies fine-tuning examples whose gradients align with unsafe behavior. By simplifying a low-rank attribution method and restricting backpropagation to the final four transformer blocks, SimpleLoRIF can embed datasets on the order of a million examples, boosting gradient attribution from a small-scale analysis tool into a practical filter for full post-training datasets. We first validate it on emergent misalignment, where we find that gradients can connect insecure-code training data to the broadly harmful behaviors that appear after fine-tuning, with AUC as high as 0.865 in the gradient space of misaligned models. We then use SimpleLoRIF to build SafeTulu, a version of Tulu 3 with the 20% of examples most gradient-aligned with unsafe responses removed. Training on SafeTulu reduces GCG attack success rate by up to 22% across Qwen, Llama, and Olmo, outperforming both LLM-as-a-judge and prior gradient-based filtering, while largely preserving or even improving capability. Finally, we analyzed the removed data and identify possibly under-studied sources of safety degradation, such as tool-execution failures and narrative arithmetic. We release SafeTulu along with a Hugging Face Space that lets researchers build their own customized versions of SafeTulu to fine-tune on, such as by changing the removal fraction or filtering only certain subsets.

ru.title: Безопасность LLM начинается с очистки данных от скрытых градиентных угроз
ru.desc: Статья представляет SimpleLoRIF — масштабируемый метод на основе градиентных эмбеддингов, который находит примеры для fine-tuning LLM, чьи градиенты согласуются с небезопасным поведением модели. Метод упрощает low-rank attribution и ограничивает backpropagation последними четырьмя трансформерными блоками, что позволяет обрабатывать датасеты около миллиона примеров. С его помощью создан датасет SafeTulu, из которого удалено 20% наиболее опасных примеров, что снижает успешность GCG-атак до 22% на моделях Qwen, Llama и Olmo без заметной потери качества. Авторы также публикуют Hugging Face Space, с помощью которого исследователи могут настраивать фильтрацию под свои задачи.

en.title: Find the Hidden Training Data That Weakens Safety
en.desc: SimpleLoRIF uses gradient alignment to find instruction-tuning examples linked to unsafe model behavior, even when the examples appear harmless. It makes gradient attribution scalable by using low-rank embeddings and backpropagating through only the final four transformer blocks. Removing the 20% of Tulu 3 examples most aligned with unsafe responses creates SafeTulu, which lowers GCG attack success by up to 22% while largely preserving or improving capabilities. The analysis also highlights overlooked sources of safety degradation, including tool-execution failures and narrative arithmetic.

zh.title: 用梯度找出隐蔽的安全风险，让微调数据更安全
zh.desc: 这篇论文提出 SimpleLoRIF，用梯度嵌入找出那些看起来无害、却可能削弱大语言模型安全性的指令数据。它简化低秩归因方法，并只对 Transformer 最后四个模块进行反向传播，因此能处理多达百万条训练样例。研究者据此从 Tulu 3 中移除与不安全回答梯度最相似的 20% 样例，构建了 SafeTulu。使用 SafeTulu 微调后，多个模型抵御 GCG 对抗攻击的效果提升，同时大体保留甚至改善原有能力。

papers.title: CEPO: A General Framework for Improving Prompt Optimization in Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: Abstract CEPO improves multi-agent prompt optimization by separating shared coordination from agent-specific execution, boosting performance across benchmarks and scaling efficiently with more agents.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Multi-agent systems (MAS) require both effective coordination and specialized task execution. Existing prompt optimization approaches typically couple these functions within agent-specific prompts. We introduce Coordinator-Executor Prompt Optimization (CEPO), a general framework for improving prompt optimization in MAS. CEPO separates system-level coordination from agent-level execution through a shared coordinator prompt and agent-specific executor prompts, and guides their updates according to their respective roles. This structure allows shared coordination rules to be refined consistently across agents while keeping execution instructions separately adjustable. CEPO provides the prompt structure and optimization guidance, while existing prompt optimizers perform the underlying search. Extensive experiments spanning 11 benchmarks across four domains demonstrate that applying CEPO to four existing prompt optimizers consistently improves their performance. Ablations and qualitative analyses support the proposed design, while controlled studies on a document-understanding MAS further demonstrate improved optimization budget efficiency and performance scaling with the number of agents.

ru.title: Координатор и исполнители: разделяй правила и задачи, чтобы улучшать промпты агентов
ru.desc: В статье предлагается CEPO — фреймворк для оптимизации промптов в мультиагентных системах (MAS), где разделяются общий координатор и исполнители для каждого агента. Координатор задаёт единые правила взаимодействия, а промпты-исполнители настраивают специфические инструкции под роль каждого агента. CEPO задаёт структуру промптов и направления их обновления, а поиск оптимальных значений выполняют существующие оптимизаторы промптов. Эксперименты на 11 бенчмарках в четырёх доменах показывают стабильный прирост качества, а также лучшую эффективность бюджета оптимизации при росте числа агентов.

en.title: Coordinate Together, Execute by Role
en.desc: CEPO is a framework for optimizing prompts in multi-agent systems. It separates shared coordination instructions into a coordinator prompt and task-specific instructions into executor prompts for individual agents. Existing prompt optimizers search for improvements while CEPO guides updates to each prompt according to its role. Experiments across 11 benchmarks show consistent gains, more efficient use of optimization budgets, and improved scaling as the number of agents increases.

zh.title: 共享协调、分工执行，让多智能体提示优化更高效
zh.desc: 本文提出协调者—执行者提示优化（CEPO）框架，用于改进多智能体系统中的提示优化。它将系统层面的协调规则放在所有智能体共享的协调者提示中，并将具体任务指令放在各智能体独立的执行者提示中。优化时，协调者提示和执行者提示会根据各自职责分别调整，而底层搜索仍由现有的提示优化器完成。在涵盖四个领域、11项基准测试的实验中，CEPO提升了四种现有优化器的表现；进一步研究也显示，它能更有效地利用优化预算，并随着智能体数量增加而扩展性能。

papers.title: Venus-DefakerOne2: A Vision-Forensics Foundation Model with Broader Coverage
papers.abstract: Abstract Venus-DefakerOne2 is a unified anti-forgery foundation model that extends detection to diverse forgery forms and media types through alternating LoRA and full-parameter tuning and entropy-based test adaptation.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Real-world forgery is inherently heterogeneous: it manifests not only as digital manipulation but also as physical spoofing, and is carried not only by images but also by videos. Despite substantial progress, a unified anti-forgery foundation model covering such a broad threat spectrum remains absent. In this paper, we present Venus-DefakerOne2, which substantially extends the forensic capability boundary along both the forgery-form and media-type dimensions. Trained on tens of millions of open-source and in-house samples, it incorporates two key designs. Tide-Style-Tuning alternates LoRA and full-parameter fine-tuning to balance computational efficiency, generalization, and hard-sample fitting while mitigating catastrophic forgetting. Entropy-based Test Adaptation determines the optimal prediction modality by analyzing prediction entropy. Venus-DefakerOne2 achieves new state-of-the-art performance across a comprehensive suite of benchmarks, including DeepFake faces (96.7%), AI-generated images (93.3%), tampered documents (87.6%), manipulated natural images (89.6%), physical spoofs (93.1%), and AI-generated videos (96.0%). It significantly outperforms both specialized expert models and its predecessor, DefakerOne, establishing itself as a powerful and versatile foundation model for binary-decision forensic tasks.
affiliations: Technical Committee on Digital Media Forensics and Security, CSIG

ru.title: Одна модель, чтобы распознать любую подделку
ru.desc: Статья представляет Venus-DefakerOne2 — унифицированную foundation model для обнаружения подделок, которая охватывает DeepFake-лица, сгенерированные AI изображения и видео, подделанные документы, физические спуфинги и манипуляции с изображениями. Модель обучена на десятках миллионов образцов и использует чередование LoRA и full-parameter fine-tuning (Tide-Style-Tuning), что balances вычислительную эффективность, обобщающую способность и сохранение знаний при catastrophic forgetting. Дополнительно применяется Entropy-based Test Adaptation, которая выбирает оптимальную модальность предсказания по энтропии выходов модели. Venus-DefakerOne2 достигает state-of-the-art результатов на широком наборе бенчмарков и превосходит как специализированные expert-модели, так и предшественника DefakerOne.

en.title: One Forensic Model to Detect Forgery Across Media
en.desc: Venus-DefakerOne2 is a unified anti-forgery foundation model that detects digital and physical forgeries across images and videos. It is trained on tens of millions of samples and uses Tide-Style-Tuning, which alternates LoRA with full-parameter fine-tuning to balance efficiency, generalization, and adaptation to difficult examples while reducing catastrophic forgetting. At test time, entropy-based adaptation selects the prediction modality based on the model’s prediction entropy. The model achieves state-of-the-art results across benchmarks for deepfakes, AI-generated media, document tampering, image manipulation, and physical spoofs.

zh.title: 跨越图像与视频，统一识别多种伪造
zh.desc: Venus-DefakerOne2 是一个统一的反伪造基础模型，可检测图像和视频中的多种数字篡改与实体伪造。它使用交替进行 LoRA 微调和全参数微调的方法，在控制计算成本的同时提升泛化能力、拟合难例，并缓解灾难性遗忘。模型还通过分析预测熵进行测试时自适应，以选择合适的预测方式。在多个基准测试中，它取得了先进表现，覆盖深度伪造人脸、AI 生成内容、篡改文档和实体伪造等任务。

papers.title: CaPtain: A Pipeline for Post-Training Code-as-Policy Robot Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract CaPtain trains small open vision-language models via supervised fine-tuning and multi-turn reinforcement learning with a physical critic to perform robot manipulation through code, achieving strong results without frontier models or vision-language-action backbones.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Across coding, web, and tool-use tasks, language-model agents are now routinely trained with the same recipe: supervised fine-tuning (SFT) to learn the interface, then multi-turn reinforcement learning (RL) to master it. Code-as-policy (CaP) casts robot manipulation in the same form, as the policy writes code against robot APIs and reads back the results, so the same recipe should apply. Yet existing CaP agents sidestep training: they either prompt closed frontier models or delegate manipulation to pre-trained vision-language-action models (VLAs) and high-level skills, while small open vision-language models (VLMs) fail outright. We present CaPtain, an open post-training pipeline that turns a small open VLM into a capable CaP agent, with no VLA, frontier model, or privileged state at test time. CaPtain trains and deploys the policy inside CaPtain-Harness, which exposes low-level perception, geometry, and guarded-motion primitives across simulation and real hardware. We first align the base model via SFT on synthetic trajectories generated with GPT-6 Astra, then apply multi-turn RL. Multi-turn RL must credit tens of agent requests, whose physical effects often surface turns later, from a single end-of-episode outcome. We therefore introduce a physical critic that reads privileged simulator state, never seen by the policy, and credits each request by how much it changes the predicted chance of success. Starting from Qwen3.5-4B (0% zero-shot), CaPtain-4B reaches 55.4% held-out LIBERO success after SFT and 73.8% after RL. On LIBERO-PRO, it reaches 78.5%, surpassing several frontier-model agents, and its RL gains persist across three perturbation suites (+17.6 to +21.2 points). Without target-domain training, it attains 83.3% on SimplerEnv WidowX, exceeds frontier models on CaP-Bench, and runs on a real robot after simulation-only adaptation. We release all code, data, and model weights.
affiliations: MMLab, The Chinese University of Hong Kong

ru.title: Маленькая открытая VLM учится управлять роботом через код и сама превосходит гигантов
ru.desc: Авторы представляют CaPtain — открытый пайплайн пост-обучения, который превращает небольшую открытую vision-language модель (VLM) в агента Code-as-Policy для манипуляций роботом. Модель сначала обучается через supervised fine-tuning на синтетических траекториях, а затем проходит multi-turn reinforcement learning. Ключевая новинка — physical critic, который использует приватное состояние симулятора, недоступное политике, и оценивает вклад каждого запроса в изменение предсказанной вероятности успеха. Итог: модель Qwen3.5-4B после обучения достигает 73.8% успеха на LIBERO и 83.3% на SimplerEnv без обучения на целевом домене, превосходя ряд агентов на frontier-моделях, и работает на реальном роботе.

en.title: Teach Small Open Models to Control Robots Through Code
en.desc: CaPtain trains a small open vision-language model to control robots by writing code that uses robot APIs. It first uses supervised fine-tuning on synthetic examples, then multi-turn reinforcement learning to improve performance. A physical critic uses hidden simulator state to estimate how each request affects the chance of task success, helping assign credit when effects appear several turns later. The resulting 4B-parameter agent achieves strong results in simulation and transfers to new settings and a real robot without relying on a vision-language-action model at test time.

zh.title: 让小型开源视觉语言模型学会用代码操控机器人
zh.desc: 这篇论文提出 CaPtain，用监督微调（SFT）和多轮强化学习（RL）训练小型开源视觉语言模型，使其通过编写代码控制机器人完成操作任务。系统提供感知、几何计算和安全运动等机器人接口，并使用物理评论器评估每次代码请求对任务成功概率的影响，从而解决结果延迟出现时的奖励分配问题。训练时评论器可以读取特权模拟器状态，但执行任务的策略无需这些信息，也不依赖视觉语言动作模型或闭源前沿模型。实验显示，CaPtain 在多个模拟基准上取得较强成绩，并能迁移到真实机器人。

papers.title: Probing Spatial State Representations in Visual Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Abstract Visual foundation models vary in supporting persistent spatial states across structure, persistence, prediction, and action, with readout accuracy not guaranteeing history-based updates or reliable goal-directed progress.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small An observer sees only part of the surrounding world, yet must keep track of what lies beyond the current view. Spatial perception therefore involves more than recognizing individual images: it calls for a persistent spatial state that is updated under self-motion and used to guide action. Do visual foundation models provide representations that support such a state? We study this question through four levels of spatial capability---spatial structure, object persistence, predictive spatial update, and actionability---using frozen-feature probes on ten representations under streaming egocentric observations of static indoor environments. The resulting capability profiles vary across tasks, network layers, and prefix lengths: strong readout of the visible scene does not ensure accurate object persistence or future-feature retrieval. Matched controls separate readout accuracy from reliance on visual history and motion. Native future prediction retains recoverable spatial structure, but a spatial reader trained on real features does not transfer to predicted features unchanged. Finally, goal-dependent candidate selection does not establish reliable continuous action utility: predicted actions respond to goal changes, yet supplying the correct goal does not reliably improve progress. Across the four levels, object persistence and actionability build on camera-pose readout, whereas feature prediction builds on visible-scene readout. Together, these findings motivate evaluating spatial representations not only by what can be decoded from them, but by whether that information is maintained beyond observation, updated predictively, and used for goal-directed action.
affiliations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong
The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

ru.title: Видеть сцену недостаточно: модели должны помнить пространство и действовать в нём
ru.desc: Статья исследует, способны ли визуальные foundation-модели формировать устойчивое пространственное состояние, необходимое для навигации и действий. Авторы проверяют четыре уровня пространственных способностей: структуру пространства, сохранение объектов, предсказание будущих признаков и пригодность для действий, используя frozen-feature probes на десяти представлениях. Результаты показывают, что хорошее считывание видимой сцены не гарантирует точного сохранения объектов и предсказания признаков, а goal-dependent выбор действий не всегда ведёт к реальному прогрессу. Авторы призывают оценивать пространственные представления не только по декодируемой информации, но и по тому, поддерживается ли она за пределами наблюдения, обновляется ли предиктивно и используется ли для целенаправленных действий.

en.title: Seeing Space Is Not Enough: Models Must Track, Predict, and Act
en.desc: This paper tests whether visual foundation models maintain useful spatial representations as an observer moves through indoor scenes. Using frozen-feature probes, it evaluates spatial structure, object persistence, predictive updates, and actionability across ten representations. Strong decoding of the visible scene does not guarantee that models track objects over time, predict future features reliably, or make actions that improve progress toward a goal. The results show that spatial representations should be evaluated by how well they preserve and update information over time and support goal-directed action, not just by what can be read from a single view.

zh.title: 空间理解不止于看见，更要记住、预测并行动
zh.desc: 这篇论文研究视觉基础模型能否在连续的第一人称观察中维持并使用空间状态。研究者用冻结特征探针，评估十种模型表征的空间结构、物体持续追踪、预测性空间更新和行动能力。结果显示，模型能识别当前画面中的场景，并不代表它能可靠地追踪视野外的物体、预测未来特征或借助目标稳定地推动行动。论文因此强调，评估空间表征不能只看信息是否可解码，还要检验模型能否跨时间保存信息、根据运动更新状态并据此行动。

papers.title: WorldBridge: Bridging Video and Action for Task Generalization in World Action Models
papers.abstract: Abstract WorldBridge improves robot task generalization by combining video prediction with sparse action supervision via separate video and action experts, achieving state-of-the-art results across manipulation benchmarks.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Achieving the broad task generalization of embodied models in physical environments remains a central challenge in robot learning. We study this challenge in World Action Models (WAMs) through two complementary capabilities: video generalization, which predicts the visual evolution of new tasks, and action generalization, which translates these predictions into executable behavior through a video-to-action bridge. By varying video and action supervision for tasks outside an initial training set, we examine their respective contributions to task transfer. On RoboTwin 2.0, using only in-distribution video-action supervision yields a 25.07% success rate on out-of-distribution tasks. Introducing videos of these tasks without their action labels raises success to 55.90%, while adding just one action-labeled demonstration per task further improves it to 70.70%. These findings suggest that broader video coverage enables task transfer by leveraging existing inverse-dynamics capabilities, while even sparse action supervision further strengthens those capabilities. Guided by this perspective, we introduce WorldBridge, a WAM with separate video and action experts connected through structured attention and trained with joint flow matching. WorldBridge incorporates visual memory at two temporal scales and action forcing, alongside a unified data processing pipeline that standardizes and filters heterogeneous robot trajectories and egocentric hand-derived supervision. Across multiple manipulation benchmarks, WorldBridge achieves state-of-the-art performance among the compared methods, including 96.23% on RoboTwin 2.0 full data setting and 80.9% on clean to random setting, 82.8% on RoboCasa GR1 TableTop, and 57.6% on DOMINO Level-1. Our study highlights the complementary roles of video prediction and action grounding in developing robots that generalize across tasks.

ru.title: Видео учит предсказывать, а несколько действий — выполнять: мост к обобщению роботов
ru.desc: Статья посвящена обобщению роботов на новые задачи с помощью World Action Models (WAM), которые объединяют предсказание видео и генерацию действий. Авторы показывают, что видео без разметки действий и даже одна размеченная демонстрация на задачу заметно повышают успешность переноса на out-of-distribution задачи. На основе этого предложен WorldBridge: WAM с отдельными видео- и action-экспертами, связанными structured attention и обученными совместным flow matching, с визуальной памятью на двух масштабах времени и унифицированным пайплайном обработки данных. Модель достигает state-of-the-art результатов на нескольких бенчмарках манипуляций, включая RoboTwin 2.0 и RoboCasa.

en.title: Teach Robots New Tasks with Videos—and Just a Few Actions
en.desc: The paper studies how robots can generalize to tasks they have not seen before by predicting videos and turning those predictions into actions. On RoboTwin 2.0, adding videos of new tasks without action labels raises success from 25.07% to 55.90%, and one action-labeled example per task raises it to 70.70%. The authors introduce WorldBridge, a World Action Model with separate video and action experts, connected by structured attention and trained jointly with flow matching. It also uses visual memory at two time scales and action forcing, and achieves strong results across several manipulation benchmarks.

zh.title: 让机器人从看懂视频到学会行动
zh.desc: 这篇论文研究机器人如何把学过的技能迁移到新任务，重点考察视频预测和动作生成两种能力。实验发现，加入新任务的视频但不提供动作标签，成功率从25.07%升至55.90%；每个任务再提供一个带动作标签的示范，成功率进一步升至70.70%。作者据此提出WorldBridge：它使用独立的视频专家和动作专家，通过结构化注意力连接，并以联合流匹配进行训练。WorldBridge还结合双时间尺度视觉记忆与动作强制机制，在多个操作基准上取得了所比较方法中的最佳表现。

papers.title: GLOW-FM: Efficient Generative Low-Light Image Enhancement with One-Step Latent Flow Matching
papers.abstract: Abstract GLOW-FM is a one-step latent flow-matching framework that enables efficient generative low-light image enhancement via single-function evaluation in a compact latent space.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Low-light image enhancement (LLIE) aims to recover well-exposed and perceptually faithful images from severely degraded observations. Recent diffusion-based generative methods achieve strong perceptual quality by leveraging powerful image priors, but their iterative sampling incurs substantial computational cost, limiting practical deployment. Despite recent efficiency gains in generative LLIE, high-quality enhancement with a single function evaluation and low overall computation remains challenging, particularly under diverse real-world low-light conditions. We introduce GLOW-FM, a one-step latent flow-matching framework for efficient generative LLIE. GLOW-FM performs conditional transport in the latent space of a frozen Tiny-VAE and leverages Terminal Velocity Matching (TVM) to enable enhancement with a single function evaluation. Matched comparisons with alternative one-step objectives support TVM as an effective design choice, and, to the best of our knowledge, this is its first adaptation to image restoration and specifically to LLIE. Extensive experiments on challenging real-world benchmarks demonstrate that GLOW-FM achieves competitive image quality and state-of-the-art cross-dataset generalization while requiring only a single function evaluation and 34 GFLOPs for the small variant. These findings highlight the potential of GLOW-FM to bring generative LLIE closer to practical deployment through single-step inference and compact latent modeling. Code will be made publicly available upon publication.

ru.title: Один шаг вместо сотен: быстрое улучшение изображений при слабом свете
ru.desc: GLOW-FM — это фреймворк на основе latent flow matching, который улучшает изображения при слабом освещении за один шаг. Модель выполняет условный перенос (conditional transport) в латентном пространстве замороженного Tiny-VAE, что делает обработку компактной. Для обучения используется Terminal Velocity Matching (TVM), который позволяет получать результат за одну function evaluation; это первая адаптация TVM для задач image restoration и LLIE. На сложных реальных бенчмарках метод показывает конкурентное качество, лучшую кросс-датасетную генерализацию и требует всего 34 GFLOPs для малого варианта, что приближает генеративный LLIE к практическому применению.

en.title: Brighten Low-Light Images in One Step
en.desc: GLOW-FM enhances low-light images using flow matching in the compact latent space of a frozen Tiny-VAE. It uses Terminal Velocity Matching to generate an enhanced image with a single function evaluation, avoiding the costly iterative sampling used by diffusion models. Experiments show competitive image quality and state-of-the-art generalization across datasets, with the small model requiring 34 GFLOPs. The results suggest that one-step latent generation can make generative low-light enhancement more practical.

zh.title: 一步推理，让暗光图像焕发清晰真实
zh.desc: GLOW-FM 是一种用于低照度图像增强的一步式潜空间流匹配框架，目标是从严重退化的暗光图像中恢复自然、曝光良好的图像。它在冻结的 Tiny-VAE 潜空间中进行条件传输，并用终端速度匹配（TVM）实现单次函数评估即可完成增强。实验表明，TVM 是有效的一步式训练目标；在真实场景基准上，该方法取得有竞争力的图像质量和先进的跨数据集泛化能力。小型版本仅需一次函数评估和 34 GFLOPs，展现了生成式低照度增强走向实际部署的潜力。

papers.title: When Requirements Interact: Scaling Long-Horizon Coding via Interdependent Specifications
papers.abstract: Abstract CodeSpecWeave synthesizes complex, interdependent software development tasks with verified tests to train coding agents, improving performance on long-horizon benchmarks.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small To succeed in real-world long-horizon software development, coding agents must satisfy multi-dimensional task specifications, such as interface compatibility and error handling, and do so without breaking existing dependencies. However, current works lack specification in both quantity and diversity, often emphasizing primary goals while ignoring complex constraints. Synthesizing tasks to bridge this gap presents two challenges: naively adding specifications risks reducing tasks to trivial checklists rather than compelling joint reasoning, and verifying these subtle interactions risks overlooking hidden flaws or rejecting valid alternatives. To address these challenges, we introduce CodeSpecWeave, a framework for synthesizing tasks with rich, interdependent specifications. Grounded in real developer seeds, a synthesis agent iteratively develops both coupled task requirements and executable tests, while a review agent audits solution trajectories from multiple models to guarantee test reliability. Using this pipeline, we construct 4,670 training tasks across 2,865 repositories. Applying Reinforcement learning on these tasks significantly improves performance over the base model on DeepSWE-v1.1, largely outperforming existing baselines. Furthermore, we curate CodeSpecWeave-Bench, a rigorous benchmark comprising 100 tasks and 1,044 specifications, which clearly separates frontier models and reveals significant headroom in handling interdependent engineering constraints.

ru.title: Учим AI-агентов писать код, который не ломает всё вокруг
ru.desc: Статья представляет CodeSpecWeave — фреймворк для автоматического синтеза задач разработки ПО с взаимозависимыми спецификациями и исполняемыми тестами, основанными на реальных seed-задачах разработчиков. Synthesis agent итеративно создаёт связанные требования и тесты, а review agent проверяет траектории решений нескольких моделей, гарантируя надёжность тестов. На основе этого пайплайна собрано 4 670 обучающих задач из 2 865 репозиториев, и обучение с помощью Reinforcement Learning заметно улучшает базовую LLM на DeepSWE-v1.1. Также авторы выпускают бенчмарк CodeSpecWeave-Bench из 100 задач и 1 044 спецификаций, который выявляет слабые места современных моделей в работе со сложными инженерными ограничениями.

en.title: Weave Real-World Constraints Into Better Coding Agents
en.desc: CodeSpecWeave creates software engineering tasks with many connected requirements, such as preserving interfaces and handling errors without breaking dependencies. A synthesis agent builds tasks and executable tests from real developer examples, while a review agent checks solution attempts to ensure the tests are reliable. The framework produces 4,670 training tasks, and reinforcement learning on them improves a model’s results on the DeepSWE-v1.1 benchmark. Its 100-task benchmark also shows that models still struggle with complex, interdependent engineering constraints.

zh.title: 编织相互依赖的规格，训练更可靠的编程智能体
zh.desc: CodeSpecWeave 是一个用于合成复杂软件开发任务的框架，帮助训练编程智能体处理长期、多约束的工程工作。它从真实开发任务出发，由生成智能体逐步编写相互关联的需求和可执行测试，再由审查智能体检查多个模型的解决过程，以提高测试的可靠性。研究者用该方法构建了包含 4,670 个任务的数据集，并通过强化学习训练模型，使其在 DeepSWE-v1.1 基准上的表现优于基础模型和现有方法。论文还发布了包含 100 个任务和 1,044 项规格的 CodeSpecWeave-Bench，用于评估模型满足相互依赖工程约束的能力。

papers.title: On the Origin and Evolution of Training-Inference Mismatch in LLM Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Abstract On-policy reinforcement learning for large language models suffers from training-inference mismatch due to numerical discrepancies and policy lag, and a derived discrepancy-lag correction stabilizes training by centering errors, clipping importance ratios, and resynchronizing sampling.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small On-policy reinforcement learning for large language models assumes that training responses are sampled from the current policy. In practice, an inference engine samples the responses and a separate trainer computes the gradients, and the training-inference mismatch between the two makes the training data off-policy. The mismatch has two sources, the numerics of the engine and the stale weights of asynchronous sampling, and a correction that stabilizes training under one source can fail under the other. We ask which property of a mismatch source decides the correction it needs. Evaluating the trainer at the sampler's weights splits each sampled-token error exactly into a numerical discrepancy of the engine and a policy lag of the trainer, and we follow both through training. The numerical discrepancy stays approximately constant, so it biases the updates by a nearly fixed amount, and centering the score at each prefix removes its leading bias. The policy lag is produced by the trainer's own updates: the bias it leaves enters the next update, which enlarges the next lag and closes a feedback loop. Importance weighting cuts this loop only while the lag ratio stays concentrated, and on Qwen3-1.7B it fails at the step where the effective sample size of the ratio falls below one half. From this account we derive the discrepancy-lag correction (DLC), which centers the numerical discrepancy, clips the lag ratio against the sampler's weights and resynchronizes the sampler when this effective sample size falls below one half. Under a stale sampler, DLC keeps the KL divergence from on-policy training within twice the KL between two independent on-policy trainings on Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3-1.7B, and its resynchronization prevents collapses that the per-token corrections leave and that a KL measured on the sampler's prefixes does not detect.

ru.title: Синхронизируй сэмплер — и обучение LLM снова станет стабильным
ru.desc: Статья рассматривает проблему рассогласования между сэмплером (inference engine) и тренером в on-policy обучении с подкреплением для LLM: численные расхождения движка и устаревание весов при асинхронной генерации (policy lag) делают данные off-policy. Авторы показывают, что численная ошибка почти постоянна и смещает обновления, и её можно убрать центрированием score на каждом префиксе, тогда как policy lag образует обратную связь, которую importance weighting сдерживает лишь пока отношение весов остаётся сконцентрированным. На основе этого предложен метод DLC (discrepancy-lag correction): центрирование численной ошибки, клиппинг отношения importance weights и ресинхронизация сэмплера, когда effective sample size падает ниже одной второй. Эксперименты на Qwen3-0.6B и Qwen3-1.7B показывают, что DLC удерживает KL-дивергенцию в пределах удвоенного KL между двумя независимыми on-policy запусками и предотвращает коллапс обучения.

en.title: Correct steady errors, control policy lag, and keep training on track
en.desc: The paper studies why on-policy reinforcement learning for large language models becomes off-policy when an inference engine generates responses and a separate trainer updates the model. It separates the mismatch into numerical discrepancy, which causes a relatively steady bias, and policy lag, which grows through feedback between updates. The proposed discrepancy-lag correction (DLC) centers numerical errors, clips importance ratios to limit policy lag, and resynchronizes sampling when the effective sample size becomes too low. Experiments on Qwen3 models show that DLC keeps training closer to on-policy behavior and prevents collapses missed by some other corrections.

zh.title: 拆解误差与滞后，让大模型强化学习更稳定
zh.desc: 这篇论文研究大语言模型进行在策略强化学习时，推理引擎与训练器之间的差异如何导致训练数据变成离策略数据。作者将这种差异分为推理引擎数值误差和训练器权重滞后，并发现前者造成近似固定的偏差，后者则会形成不断加剧的反馈循环。为此，论文提出差异—滞后校正（DLC）：按前缀中心化数值误差、裁剪滞后策略的重要性比率，并在有效样本量低于阈值时重新同步采样器。在 Qwen3 实验中，DLC 能更稳定地贴近在策略训练，并避免其他逐 token 校正可能遗漏的训练崩溃。

papers.title: HALO: Human-Grounded Granular Evaluation of Proactive Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract HALO introduces a human-annotated benchmark and dataset to evaluate proactive agents, revealing that over-proactivity is the dominant failure mode.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Proactive agents must decide whether, when, and how far to assist without an explicit request. Existing evaluations often rely on automated scores or binary verdicts, offering limited human diagnosis of evidence use and intervention quality. To address these gaps, we introduce HALO, Human-Grounded GrAnular EvaLuation of PrOactive Agents. HALO-Arena covers 4 proactive need types, Dependency, Blockage, Risk, and Opportunity, across 10 everyday domains and 50 personal environments. Scenarios require agents to retrieve evidence from structured databases or unstructured documents before judging whether assistance is warranted and choosing its scope. On HALO-Arena, we construct HALO-8K, a dataset of 8,000 responses from 10 models across 400 scenarios, annotated by 20 experts for action level, acceptability verdicts, and human diagnosis. For rejected responses, human diagnosis covers timing, intensity, and other issues. Recorded reasoning tokens and retrieval rounds measure the effort behind these responses. The best proprietary and open-source models achieve 72.88% and 56.63% acceptability, respectively. Our central finding is that over-proactivity is the dominant observed failure mode, with Premature timing or Excessive intensity accounting for 61.20% of rejected responses. Further analyses yield complementary findings on the balance between intervention and restraint, evidence acquisition, and the calibration of timing and intensity.

ru.title: Агенты чаще мешают, чем помогают: главная беда — чрезмерная проактивность
ru.desc: Статья представляет HALO — бенчмарк и датасет для оценки проактивных AI-агентов, которые решают, помогать ли пользователю без явного запроса. Авторы собрали HALO-Arena с 400 сценариями в 4 типах потребностей и 10 доменах и разметили 8 000 ответов 10 LLM экспертами по уровню действия, приемлемости и диагнозу ошибок. Лучшие модели показывают 72.88% приемлемости у проприетарных и 56.63% у открытых моделей. Главный вывод: доминирующая ошибка — чрезмерная проактивность (преждевременное вмешательство или избыточная интенсивность), которая составляет 61.20% отклонённых ответов.

en.title: Proactive agents must know when to step in—and when to hold back
en.desc: HALO introduces a human-annotated benchmark for evaluating proactive agents, which decide whether and how to help without an explicit request. Its HALO-Arena benchmark tests agents on four types of needs across everyday scenarios that require retrieving evidence from databases or documents. HALO-8K contains 8,000 model responses, labeled by experts for action level, acceptability, and issues such as timing and intensity. The results show that over-proactivity is the most common failure: premature or overly intense interventions account for 61.20% of rejected responses.

zh.title: 主动帮助要有度：该出手时出手，也要懂得克制
zh.desc: HALO提出了一个由人工标注的基准和数据集，用来评估主动型智能体在没有明确请求时是否能适时提供帮助。HALO-Arena涵盖4类需求、10个日常领域和50种个人环境，要求智能体先从数据库或文档中检索证据，再决定是否介入以及介入到什么程度。研究人员构建了包含8,000条模型回答的HALO-8K，并由专家标注行动等级、可接受性和错误原因，以更细致地分析智能体的表现。结果显示，过度主动是最常见的失败模式；被拒绝的回答中，61.20%存在介入过早或干预过度的问题。

papers.title: Supervising the Visible State: Separating Representation from View Selection in Streaming Video
papers.abstract: Abstract Visible-State Supervision and Test-Time Causal View Search improve streaming action recognition by separating representation learning from evidence selection, boosting accuracy with fewer frames.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small An action seen once and the same action seen three times receive the same action-recognition label, so that supervision does not require a model to count. Answers shared across histories that differ in event order, accumulation, or relations leave those distinctions unconstrained; we call this state under-specification. Visible-State Supervision (ViSS) addresses it by training on source-grounded probes of event identity, order, accumulation, relation change, and answer sufficiency; under the same recent-frame interface it improves OVO-Bench over a strict-matched generic temporal supervision baseline while remaining comparable on StreamingBench, with the largest gain in hallucination detection. Test-Time Causal View Search (TVS) then adapts evidence access while keeping the learned model fixed, expanding from recent frames to sparse event and compact history views on demand. The two interventions separate representation from view selection: supervision particularly benefits hallucination detection and causal reasoning, access particularly benefits event recall and forward reasoning. Together they reach the best reported accuracy among the published systems compared here on StreamingBench and OVO-Bench at a fraction of the processed frames of exhaustive selection, and strict replay shows that most of the remaining gap to a three-view oracle is a correct answer that was later replaced.
